- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; apply a 5–10% downward correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day ahead forecasts are prone to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag adjustment downward for short-term (1–3d) forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
